mission: The technical AGI safety teams at Google DeepMind (AGI Safety & Alignment, led by Rohin Shah under Anca Dragan, plus mechanistic interpretability led by Neel Nanda) work on preventing misuse and misalignment of future AGI. They co-author the Frontier Safety Framework, which sets 'Critical Capability Levels' at which extra safeguards are required, and the 2025 paper 'An Approach to Technical AGI Safety & Security'. Shane Legg chairs the internal AGI Safety Council. Founded year is approximate (DeepMind's safety team dates to ~2016).

key_work.title: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety & Security
key_work.plain_summary: A ~100-page plan covering four risk areas — misuse, misalignment, accidents and structural risks — with most detail on blocking misuse and on making AI pursue the goals humans intend.

key_work.title: Frontier Safety Framework v3 (and v3.1, Apr 2026)
key_work.plain_summary: Their company risk policy: added a harmful-manipulation threshold, protocols for models that could resist shutdown or speed AI R&D, safety-case reviews before launches and large internal deployments, and in 2026 lower 'Tracked Capability Levels' as early warnings.

key_work.title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities
key_work.plain_summary: A test suite for persuasion, cyber-offence, self-proliferation and self-reasoning abilities, run on Gemini models.

key_work.title: Gemma Scope
key_work.plain_summary: An open set of sparse autoencoders for Gemma 2 models so outside researchers can study model internals.

key_work.title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval
key_work.plain_summary: Trains agents to optimise only short-term steps that a human overseer approves, which reduced multi-step reward hacking in their experiments.

key_work.title: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
key_work.plain_summary: A widely cited collection of examples where AI systems satisfied the letter of their objective but not its spirit.

people.role: Co-founder & Chief AGI Scientist; chairs AGI Safety Council

warnings.text: AGI 'could be here within the coming years', and even a small possibility of harm from a technology this powerful must be taken seriously (Taking a responsible path to AGI, 2025).
Deceptive alignment: an AI could realise its goals differ from its instructions and deliberately try to bypass safety measures.
Future misaligned models might interfere with operators' ability to direct, modify or shut them down (FSF v3).
Models that accelerate AI R&D to destabilising levels pose both misuse and misalignment risk, including during large internal deployments (FSF v3).
Models with powerful manipulative capabilities could be misused to change beliefs and behaviour at severe scale (harmful manipulation CCL).

recommendations.text: Run early-warning dangerous-capability evaluations and apply safeguards before Critical Capability Levels are reached (FSF).
Conduct safety-case reviews before external launches — and large internal deployments — once relevant CCLs are reached (FSF v3).
Restrict access to dangerous capabilities and harden model-weight security against theft (AGI safety approach).
Use amplified oversight (e.g. debate), robust training and AI monitors that flag uncertain actions for review.
Invest in interpretability and designs that keep AI planning understandable to humans (e.g. MONA); coordinate via the Frontier Model Forum and AI Safety Institutes.
